correctness.rationale: For an irreducible sextic with the specified five ordinary nodes, the center is the unique node incident to both three-node diagonal lines, while four peripheral nodes form a projective frame. Therefore every embedded projective automorphism injects into the eight permutations preserving opposite-pair incidence; the four coordinate sign changes are always present. An additional antidiagonal element must act on the tangent cone U(Y²−Z²) with λ^4=1, multiplier μ=−λ^{-2}; λ²=1 would make its projective fixed line a component, violating integrality, leaving λ²=−1, μ=1. Substitution (s,t)→(−t,−s) gives exactly G=−A,D=−B,H=C4, proving necessity and sufficiency of D8. Independent SymPy Groebner computations on the two rational explicit examples gave only (s,t)=(1,−1), Hessian determinants 20 and 28, correct axis restrictions, squarefree infinity, and swap symmetry only for ε=0. Bézout/reducedness exclude reducibility; genus=10−5=5; Riemann–Hurwitz gives quotient genera 2,2,1 and Howe parameter r=4. Examples are over C; classification works over odd characteristic under the stipulated existence/nodal assumptions. The finite computations do not certify the universal stabilizer theorem, which rests on the incidence-and-tangent argument.
